raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

Qwen3's native CUDA decode path launches QK normalization and RoPE separately. Reuse the existing table-based QK-norm/RoPE kernel to perform both operations in place, eliminating one launch per layer and the intervening Q/K write/read without introducing a new kernel.

On Qwen3-8B, this removes 36 launches per decode step. Eight paired B200 runs before merging main measured ~1.76% lower decode latency at concurrency 1 and ~0.81% at concurrency 32. 


## Modifications

- Add an opt-in `match_cuda` mode to `table_qk_norm_rope_`. It reproduces the separate CUDA kernels' reduction order, reciprocal square root, intermediate BF16 rounding, and RoPE multiply/FMA ordering. The existing default mode remains unchanged for existing callers.
- Route eligible Qwen3 native CUDA decode through this mode under the existing `--enable-fused-qk-norm-rope` flag. Supported inputs are BF16 QKV and norm weights, head dimensions 64/128/256, equal Q/K epsilon, and standard full-head NeoX rotary embeddings. The launcher validates layouts and devices before accessing pointers.
- Preserve the separate normalization/RoPE path for prefill, target verification, unsupported head dimensions/dtypes/rotary configurations, deterministic/on-policy configurations, and the prefill Inductor configuration. V and KV-cache writes are unchanged. No Q FP8 quantization is added.
- Add focused kernel and real-constructor/model-dispatch tests, including changing-input CUDA-graph replay. Two production files: +96/-15 lines; two test files: 259 lines.

## Accuracy Tests

Local validation on NVIDIA B200, PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130, Triton 3.8.0, CUDA 13.0:

### Post-merge correctness

Tested head: `9a11fd65f8a3e17dc9b476e9521c7668ac0a1ec2`, after merging main at `15d39bd8406bc75d2b1c82c5013cd0eb36368608`. All four PR files are byte-identical to feature commit `d79827f79cce6c110950c8265278031d5eec74b2`.

- **121 tests passed in 18.02 seconds**, with no failures/skips: 28 new kernel cases + 16 new model cases + 77 existing QK-norm/RoPE cases = 121. Existing suites used their CI-sized ranges. Coverage includes exact CUDA-reference comparisons, empty/padded rows, int32/int64 positions, long positions, exceptional values, preserved V/padding, invalid inputs, dispatch exclusions, and CUDA-graph replay.

### Additional pre-merge validation 

The results below were collected before the main merge, on the production code committed as `d79827f79c` with base `e22a530859`. These checks have not been repeated on `9a11fd65f8`:

- Negative controls caught both intentionally disabled CUDA-matching arithmetic and an intentionally disabled fused dispatch. These controls ran only in local subprocess memory.
- Additional numerical stress: 735 comparisons over 1,236,967,424 Q/K values, including repeated/replay comparisons. Zero bit mismatches for non-NaNs; NaN masks also matched. NaN payload bits are not part of the contract.
- Compute Sanitizer memcheck/synccheck reported zero errors; racecheck reported zero hazards.
- Live A/B: identical token IDs, text, logprobs, and top-5 results over 16,576 generated tokens. Another 192 fixed-prefix probes matched first-decode tokens/logprobs/top-20.
- Full GSM8K: **1,233/1,319 (93.480%) in both variants**, with all 1,319 generations identical and no request errors/truncations.

Run the focused and existing regression suites from the repository root in a compatible CUDA environment:

```bash
SGLANG_IS_IN_CI=1 SGLANG_JIT_KERNEL_RUN_FULL_TESTS=0 \
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 PYTHONPATH="$PWD/python" \
python -m pytest -q \
  test/registered/kernels/ops/attention/test_table_qk_norm_rope.py \
  test/registered/unit/models/test_qwen3_qk_norm_rope.py \
  test/registered/kernels/ops/layernorm/test_qknorm.py \
  test/registered/kernels/ops/attention/test_rope.py
```

These are local GPU results, not remote CI results. H100 remains untested.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

**Historical, pre-merge measurements.** Baseline: `e22a53085994a68aaecbd7a109c8de6da32baeda`; fused production code matches feature commit `d79827f79cce6c110950c8265278031d5eec74b2`. The timings and profiles below have not been rerun on post-merge head `9a11fd65f8`. The 121-test post-merge pass above establishes focused correctness coverage, not a new performance result.

Same model revision, environment, flags, request shapes, and seed for the two measured variants:

- NVIDIA B200, TP1, `Qwen/Qwen3-8B-FP8@220b46e3b2180893580a4454f21f22d3ebb187d3`.
- FP8 weights with DeepGEMM; **BF16 activations and KV cache**; TRTLLM MHA.
- Decode CUDA graphs enabled; prefill CUDA graphs disabled.
- Eight fixed AB/BA pairs (16 fresh servers); 1,024 input / 512 output tokens at concurrency 1 and 32. Separate prefill requests used 1,024 input / 1 output token.
- Decode metric: window median first-to-last-token latency divided by 511. Reported latencies are geometric means of window medians; confidence intervals use paired log ratios across the eight pairs, not individual requests as independent repetitions.
- Quality evaluation and profiling were outside timing windows. No trials were dropped. All 10,752 measured requests completed without errors or prefix-cache hits.

Positive reduction means faster:

Results on PR commit `0492f96df9` versus baseline `4517a5ff1b`, using Qwen3-8B-FP8 on B200. Positive latency reduction means faster.

| Workload | Baseline | Fused | Latency reduction | Paired 95% interval |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Decode C1 TPOT | 2.94040 ms | 2.88819 ms | 1.776% | [1.769%, 1.782%] |
| Decode C32 TPOT | 4.29953 ms | 4.26854 ms | 0.721% | [0.556%, 0.885%] |
| Prefill C1 TTFT — controlled follow-up | 35.82999 ms | 35.66697 ms | 0.455% | [-0.085%, 0.992%] |
| Prefill C32 TTFT | 323.04991 ms | 322.70180 ms | 0.108% | [-0.502%, 0.714%] |

Decode and prefill C32 results use eight AB/BA pairs. Prefill C1 comes from a separate, CPU-affinity-controlled follow-up: 24 AB/BA pairs, 48 fresh servers, and 49,152 measured requests. Both experiments tested the same commits; results were not pooled. Statistics use paired server-window medians, not individual requests as independent repetitions.

Decode improved in all eight pairs at both concurrency levels.

Prefill C32 and the controlled C1 follow-up meet the 1% non-regression threshold. The C1 follow-up’s upper 95% slowdown bound is +0.085%. A supplementary same-resident A/A/B test covered 34,560 forwards across three sessions; all passed, with a worst upper 95% slowdown bound of +0.173%.

The follow-up completed with zero request errors, zero cached prompt tokens, and matching paired outputs. The earlier unpinned C1 result remained inconclusive; these controlled results do not establish neutrality for every deployment or prove that the earlier variation was entirely noise. No prefill speedup is claimed.



Profiler engagement checks:

- Prefill: both variants launch 288 separate QK-norm and 288 separate RoPE kernels, no combined kernels, and 4,968 total kernel events.
- One initial prefill plus eight decode steps: baseline has 324 norm + 324 RoPE launches; this change has 36 norm + 36 RoPE launches for prefill and 288 combined decode launches. Total kernel events fall from 4,813 to 4,525: **36 fewer launches per decode step**. KV writes remain separate.

Server configuration used in both variants:

```bash
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 PYTHONPATH="$PWD/python" \
python -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model-path Qwen/Qwen3-8B-FP8 \
  --revision 220b46e3b2180893580a4454f21f22d3ebb187d3 \
  --dtype bfloat16 --tp-size 1 \
  --fp8-gemm-backend deep_gemm --attention-backend trtllm_mha \
  --mem-fraction-static 0.3 --random-seed 42 \
  --host 127.0.0.1 --port 30119 \
  --enable-fused-qk-norm-rope \
  --cuda-graph-bs-decode 1 2 4 8 16 32 \
  --cuda-graph-backend-prefill disabled
```

## Checklist

- [ ] Run the full repository pre-commit suite. Ruff, Ruff format, isort, test-registry/entrypoint checks, and `git diff --check` passed locally; the complete pre-commit suite has not run.
- [x] Add focused unit/kernel regression tests.
- [ ] Update documentation if requested; this reuses an existing flag and operator.
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed results, including the unresolved prefill caveat.
- [x] Follow existing SGLang code/test conventions.
- [ ] Investigate the failed CI run badges and obtain green required checks; resolve the C1 prefill non-regression uncertainty before claiming blanket merge readiness.

+import sys
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+
+from sglang.kernels.ops.attention.rope import apply_rope_inplace
+from sglang.kernels.ops.attention.table_qk_norm_rope import table_qk_norm_rope_
+from sglang.kernels.ops.layernorm.norm import fused_inplace_qknorm
+from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_cuda_ci
+
+register_cuda_ci(est_time=30, stage="base-b-kernel-unit", runner_config="1-gpu-large")
+register_cuda_ci(est_time=30, stage="base-b-kernel-unit", runner_config="4-gpu-b200")
+
+
+def separate(qkv, positions, qw, kw, cache, hq, hk, d, eps):
+    q, k, _ = qkv.split([hq * d, hk * d, hk * d], dim=-1)
+    q, k = q.view(qkv.shape[0], hq, d), k.view(qkv.shape[0], hk, d)
+    fused_inplace_qknorm(q, k, qw, kw, eps)
+    apply_rope_inplace(q, k, cache, positions, is_neox=True)
+
+
+def assert_same_bits(actual, expected):
+    # NaN payload bits are not part of the contract; signed zero is.
+    nan = torch.isnan(expected)
+    assert torch.equal(torch.isnan(actual), nan)
+    assert torch.equal(actual.view(torch.int16)[~nan], expected.view(torch.int16)[~nan])
+
+
+def inputs(d, batch, hq, hk, seed, padded=False, position_dtype=torch.int64):
+    torch.manual_seed(seed)
+    width = (hq + 2 * hk) * d
+    storage = torch.randn(
+        batch, width + 16 * padded, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16
+    )
+    x = storage[:, 8:-8] if padded else storage
+    qw = (1 + torch.randn(d, device="cuda") * 0.2).bfloat16()
+    kw = (1 + torch.randn(d, device="cuda") * 0.2).bfloat16()
+    inv_freq = 1 / (10000 ** (torch.arange(0, d, 2, device="cuda").float() / d))
+    angles = torch.arange(131072, device="cuda").float()[:, None] * inv_freq[None, :]
+    cache = torch.cat((angles.cos(), angles.sin()), dim=-1)
+    positions = ((torch.arange(batch, device="cuda") * 7919 + seed) % 131072).to(
+        position_dtype
+    )
+    return storage, x, positions, qw, kw, cache
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("d", [64, 128, 256])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    "batch,hq,hk,padded,pos_dtype",
+    [
+        (0, 8, 2, False, torch.int64),
+        (1, 32, 8, False, torch.int64),
+        (4, 8, 2, True, torch.int32),
+        (32, 32, 8, False, torch.int64),
+        (257, 7, 1, True, torch.int64),
+    ],
+)
+def test_cuda_sequence_is_bit_exact(d, batch, hq, hk, padded, pos_dtype):
+    """Replacing CUDA norm then RoPE must preserve their bytes and untouched V/padding."""
+    storage, x, pos, qw, kw, cache = inputs(d, batch, hq, hk, 19, padded, pos_dtype)
+    before = storage.clone()
+    expected = x.clone()
+    # The table operator's empty-input guard is a no-op; the CUDA reference
+    # launcher itself does not accept an empty grid.
+    if batch:
+        separate(expected, pos, qw, kw, cache, hq, hk, d, 1e-6)
+    table_qk_norm_rope_(x, pos, qw, kw, cache, hq, hk, d, 1e-6, match_cuda=True)
+    assert_same_bits(x, expected)
+    if padded:
+        assert_same_bits(storage[:, :8], before[:, :8])
+        assert_same_bits(storage[:, -8:], before[:, -8:])
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("d", [64, 128, 256])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("eps", [1e-6, 1e-5])
+def test_extreme_values_and_rounding(d, eps):
+    """Reduction ordering and rounding must survive small/large magnitudes and NaNs."""
+    _, x, pos, qw, kw, cache = inputs(d, 128, 32, 8, 23)
+    magnitudes = torch.logspace(-20, 20, 128, device="cuda")
+    x.copy_((x.float() * magnitudes[:, None]).bfloat16())
+    x[0].zero_()
+    x[1].fill_(-0.0)
+    x[2, 0] = float("inf")
+    x[3, d] = float("nan")
+    x[4, 0] = -float("inf")
+    expected = x.clone()
+    separate(expected, pos, qw, kw, cache, 32, 8, d, eps)
+    table_qk_norm_rope_(x, pos, qw, kw, cache, 32, 8, d, eps, match_cuda=True)
+    assert_same_bits(x, expected)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("d", [64, 128, 256])
+def test_inplace_repeated_large_grid(d):
+    """Repeated launches catch unsynchronized reads/stores across warps."""
+    _, x, pos, qw, kw, cache = inputs(d, 513, 32, 8, 19)
+    torch.manual_seed(20261023)
+    x.normal_()
+    qw.copy_((0.1 + 10 * torch.rand(d, device="cuda")).bfloat16())
+    kw.copy_((0.1 + 10 * torch.rand(d, device="cuda")).bfloat16())
+    pos.random_(0, len(cache))
+    expected = x.clone()
+    separate(expected, pos, qw, kw, cache, 32, 8, d, 1e-6)
+    for _ in range(10):
+        actual = x.clone()
+        table_qk_norm_rope_(actual, pos, qw, kw, cache, 32, 8, d, 1e-6, match_cuda=True)
+        assert_same_bits(actual, expected)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("invalid", ["dtype", "qkv_stride", "table", "positions"])
+def test_cuda_mode_rejects_invalid_inputs(invalid):
+    """Malformed typed/strided inputs must fail before raw-pointer addressing."""
+    _, x, pos, qw, kw, cache = inputs(128, 4, 8, 2, 19)
+    if invalid == "dtype":
+        qw = qw.float()
+    elif invalid == "qkv_stride":
+        x = x[:, ::2]
+    elif invalid == "table":
+        cache = cache.bfloat16()
+    else:
+        pos = pos.float()
+    with pytest.raises(AssertionError):
+        table_qk_norm_rope_(x, pos, qw, kw, cache, 8, 2, 128, 1e-6, match_cuda=True)
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    sys.exit(pytest.main([__file__]))

+"""Model dispatch and changing-input graph replay; kernel numerics are tested separately."""
+
+import sys
+from types import SimpleNamespace
+from unittest.mock import patch
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+
+from sglang.srt.environ import envs
+from sglang.srt.layers.rotary_embedding import factory
+from sglang.srt.model_executor.cuda_graph_config import CudaGraphConfig, PhaseConfig
+from sglang.srt.model_executor.forward_batch_info import ForwardMode
+from sglang.srt.models import qwen3
+from sglang.srt.runtime_context import get_context, get_parallel
+from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_cuda_ci
+
+register_cuda_ci(est_time=30, stage="base-b", runner_config="1-gpu-large")
+pytestmark = pytest.mark.skipif(not torch.cuda.is_available(), reason="CUDA required")
+
+
+@pytest.fixture(autouse=True)
+def runtime():
+    defaults = dict(
+        enable_fused_qk_norm_rope=True,
+        bf16_gemm_backend="torch",
+        cuda_graph_config=CudaGraphConfig(),
+    )
+    with (
+        torch.inference_mode(),
+        get_context().override_server_args(**defaults),
+        get_parallel().override(attn_tp_size=1, attn_tp_group=None, tp_group=None),
+        envs.SGLANG_ENABLE_DETERMINISTIC_INFERENCE.override(False),
+        patch.dict(factory._ROPE_DICT, clear=True),
+    ):
+        torch.manual_seed(19)
+        yield defaults
+
+
+def make_layer(d=128, dtype=torch.bfloat16, **kwargs):
+    layer = qwen3.Qwen3Attention(
+        hidden_size=8 * d,
+        num_heads=8,
+        num_kv_heads=2,
+        head_dim=d,
+        rms_norm_eps=1e-6,
+        max_position_embeddings=4096,
+        **kwargs,
+    )
+    # Moving model parameters must not downcast the FP32 RoPE table.
+    cache = layer.rotary_emb.cos_sin_cache.cuda()
+    layer = layer.to("cuda", dtype)
+    layer.rotary_emb.cos_sin_cache = cache
+    for name, weight in layer.named_parameters():
+        weight.normal_(std=0.05)
+        if "norm" in name:
+            weight.add_(1)
+    return layer
+
+
+def separate(layer, positions, x, batch):
+    with patch.object(layer, "use_table_qk_norm_rope", False):
+        return layer.forward_prepare_native(positions, x, batch)
+
+
+def assert_same_qkv(actual, expected):
+    for got, ref in zip(actual, expected, strict=True):
+        assert torch.equal(got.view(torch.int16), ref.view(torch.int16))
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    "mode,dtype,should_fuse",
+    [
+        (ForwardMode.DECODE, torch.bfloat16, True),
+        (ForwardMode.EXTEND, torch.bfloat16, False),
+        (ForwardMode.TARGET_VERIFY, torch.bfloat16, False),
+        (ForwardMode.DECODE, torch.float16, False),
+    ],
+)
+def test_model_dispatch(mode, dtype, should_fuse):
+    layer = make_layer(dtype=dtype)
+    assert layer.use_table_qk_norm_rope
+    x = torch.randn(4, layer.hidden_size, device="cuda", dtype=dtype)
+    positions = torch.arange(4, device="cuda") + 17
+    batch = SimpleNamespace(forward_mode=mode)
+    expected = separate(layer, positions, x, batch)
+    # Only attention itself is stubbed: construction, projections, norm and RoPE are real.
+    with (
+        patch.object(layer.attn, "forward", side_effect=lambda q, *a, **kw: q) as attn,
+        patch.object(
+            qwen3, "table_qk_norm_rope_", wraps=qwen3.table_qk_norm_rope_
+        ) as fused,
+    ):
+        layer(positions, x, batch)
+    assert fused.call_count == int(should_fuse)
+    if should_fuse:
+        assert fused.call_args.kwargs["match_cuda"] is True
+    assert_same_qkv(attn.call_args.args[:3], expected)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    "settings,layer_args,deterministic_env",
+    [
+        ({"enable_fused_qk_norm_rope": False}, {}, False),
+        ({"enable_deterministic_inference": True}, {}, False),
+        ({"rl_on_policy_target": "fsdp"}, {}, False),

+            {

+                    prefill=PhaseConfig(tc_compiler="inductor")

+            },
+            {},
+            False,

+        ({}, {"d": 512}, False),
+        ({}, {"rope_scaling": {"rope_type": "linear", "factor": 2.0}}, False),
+        ({}, {}, True),
+    ],
+)
+def test_constructor_exclusions(runtime, settings, layer_args, deterministic_env):
+    with (
+        get_context().override_server_args(**{**runtime, **settings}),
+        envs.SGLANG_ENABLE_DETERMINISTIC_INFERENCE.override(deterministic_env),
+    ):
+        assert not make_layer(**layer_args).use_table_qk_norm_rope
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("batch_size", [1, 4])
+def test_changing_input_graph_replay(batch_size):
+    layer = make_layer()
+    x = torch.randn(batch_size, layer.hidden_size, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+    positions = torch.arange(batch_size, device="cuda")
+    batch = SimpleNamespace(forward_mode=ForwardMode.DECODE)
+    layer.forward_prepare_native(positions, x, batch)  # JIT warmup before capture.
+    graph = torch.cuda.CUDAGraph()
+    with (
+        patch.object(
+            qwen3, "table_qk_norm_rope_", wraps=qwen3.table_qk_norm_rope_
+        ) as fused,
+        torch.cuda.graph(graph),
+    ):
+        actual = layer.forward_prepare_native(positions, x, batch)
+    fused.assert_called_once()
+    for offset in (0, 17, 2048):
+        x.normal_()
+        positions.copy_(torch.arange(batch_size, device="cuda") + offset)
+        graph.replay()
+        assert_same_qkv(actual, separate(layer, positions, x, batch))
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    sys.exit(pytest.main([__file__]))
